bug_semantics: devalue.parse accepts attacker-controlled flattened JSON and sends it to unflatten. For the SPARSE encoding [-7, length, index, value, ...], the vulnerable parser passed the untrusted declared length directly to new Array(length). On V8, many small payload entries with large declared lengths can therefore trigger eager contiguous backing-store allocations far exceeding the input size and exhaust process memory, causing denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 introduced the SPARSE wire format and its parse branch. The branch first read value[1] as len and immediately executed new Array(len), coupling untrusted serialized metadata to eager allocation without a sparse-allocation strategy. The exact SPARSE branch and allocation are absent from its immediate parent 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c.

evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-77vg-94rm-hx3p and the PUBLISHED CVE.org record CVE-2026-42570 describe remotely reachable excessive memory consumption in devalue.parse for sparse-array deserialization, affect >=5.6.3 and <5.8.1, and identify 5.8.1 as patched.

The public BIC object has exactly one parent, 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c. Its aggregate 'Merge commit from fork' message lists development subjects, but exact subject searches over all validated-clone refs recover no separate member SHA for the introducing SPARSE parser change, so the first surviving public object cannot be decomposed further.

Tag topology verifies the advisory boundary: 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 is an ancestor of v5.6.3 (tag target a4a37d208a4d1bdd0d58c82e5644c87cab855259) but not v5.6.2 (fcf4e88275f2e2e45b9ea70ffaa5247c8f55f057).

Direct fix 206ca6712fbc380a4571c59de9ab04b91110792d replaces new Array(len) with an initially empty array, forces dictionary-elements mode by touching and deleting MAX_ARRAY_INDEX, hydrates supplied entries, and assigns array.length only afterward; its regression test documents payloads whose implied eager allocation is about 20 GB.

The direct fix parent is 14933f78ff6b712829162628682b0a1993e75d19, the v5.8.0 tag target, and still contains src/parse.js:226 const array = new Array(len). The fix is an ancestor of v5.8.1 (tag target 796ea83a76eb7e0f2af376f9c2c875f1d057f50f) but not v5.8.0.
